extracted.intended_audience: fiction writers considering PEN/Faulkner submission; literary authors, jurors, and program administrators
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and procedural rules used by PEN/Faulkner's three writer-judges to evaluate American-published fiction for longlist, shortlist, and winner selection. Covers eligibility, process, and recurring aesthetic qualities jurors cite when naming finalists and winners.

rubrics_metrics.name: Process: three-judge peer jury and selection stages
rubrics_metrics.description: Three judges (writers) chosen annually by the Board to ensure independence from commercial influence; judges select a longlist of 10, then a shortlist of 5 finalists, then one winner ('first among equals').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasizes that selection is peer-driven and proceeds in stages (longlist → shortlist → winner). The phrasing 'first among equals' suggests the winner is chosen from a tightly competitive finalist group rather than by wide quantitative margins.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility: American authorship and publication window
rubrics_metrics.description: Author must be American citizen or permanent resident; work must be published in the calendar year; any fictional form (novel, novella, story collection) is eligible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are procedural, not aesthetic, requirements — submissions failing these conditions are ineligible regardless of literary quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Beauty (sentence-level distinction)
rubrics_metrics.description: "Vital, brilliant" prose; sentence-level distinction; the work as art-object.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Foundation's recurring juror citations prize the craftsmanship of sentences and the work's aesthetic presence as an art object. Evaluate for musicality, precision, and exemplary sentence-level writing rather than mere plot or concept.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compassion / imaginative empathy
rubrics_metrics.description: The capacity to extend imaginative empathy across difference; repeatedly cited as a binding quality of finalists.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Jurors look for works that imaginatively inhabit others' lives and perspectives with ethical seriousness; lack of empathy or flattening of characters is an anti-pattern.

rubrics_metrics.name: Imagination (originality of conception)
rubrics_metrics.description: Originality of conception. Not novelty for its own sake but genuine inventive power.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether a work presents an inventive, generative premise or approach. Mere gimmickry or novelty that doesn't produce depth is discouraged.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quiet Artistry (restraint and depth)
rubrics_metrics.description: A recurring phrase distinguishing selected works: favors restraint and depth over spectacle; distinguishes works that don't 'announce themselves loudly.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preference for subtle, controlled craft — quiet, disciplined execution — rather than loud theatricality or showy effects. Works that prioritize restraint and sustained depth are favored.

rubrics_metrics.name: Humanity (engagement with the human core)
rubrics_metrics.description: Engagement with what is fundamentally human: 'drawing us into humanity's complex core of beauty, violence, joy, intelligence, and imagination.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate how the work grapples with essential human experiences and emotions; looks for breadth and seriousness in treating human life rather than superficial depiction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Complexity (capacity to hold contradictions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Refusal of simple moral or political resolutions; the capacity to hold contradictions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Jurors prize works that resist reductive conclusions and can contain ambiguous, contradictory elements. Avoid works that resolve complexity into facile moralizing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Peer-juried / craft-emphatic orientation
rubrics_metrics.description: The PEN/Faulkner is peer-juried by writers (not editors or critics), producing a craft-emphatic standard — judges read as practitioners.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compared to awards that include critics, librarians, or booksellers, PEN/Faulkner tends toward the formally distinguished and the quietly profound. Submissions should be assessed with an emphasis on craft and formal achievement as fellow writers would value them.
